propositions: A new plan-review LLM criterion ac-process-gate must flag acceptance criteria whose completion predicate is a generic, ticket-agnostic mechanical gate (children-closed, tests/CI/build/lint pass, plan-review passes, completion-verifier passes, merged/landed, commit-trailer/DCO present) that any CI or rebar enforces structurally for every ticket regardless of subject.

The ac-process-gate criterion must pass (accept without finding) acceptance criteria that name or depend on the specific ticket's deliverable — artifact, behavior, contract, test, doc, config, or criterion — even when those deliverables are tests, CI, or plan-review themselves (e.g. 'E2E tests covering feature X' or 'plan-review criteria updated to rubric Y').

The ac-process-gate criterion is routed as a 1-TURN, non-code-grounded, advisory (not blocking) plan-review criterion in the ac-text-quality facet, applied at container and leaf scopes, with a checklist of two sub-answers: not-applicable → PASS when no ACs exist, and per-AC judgment of ticket-specificity.

The rubric prompt file plan_review_ac_process_gate.md must document the advisory posture, enumerate the reject-set and accept-set, state the 'reads identically on arbitrary unrelated ticket' litmus test, and apply an err-toward-silence anti-false-positive rule.

The bounded-sanity eval corpus plan-review-ac-process-gate.eval.yaml must contain 2–8 cases with ≥2 process-gate fires and ≥2 deliverable passes, verified live via rebar criteria eval with kappa=1.0 and committed to ac_process_gate_sanity.json.

The registry chunk_by_facet packer was refactored from hardcoded chunking (which stranded singleton chunks at counts 7,13,19,25,31,37) to a balanced ceil(n/size) algorithm guaranteeing [2,size] contiguous chunks, and stale hard-coded criteria COUNT references were removed from docs and registry docstrings.
